problem.claim: How to discover and use action-sequence options autonomously for planning in complex reinforcement-learning environments.

gap.claim: Prior work focused on predefined options or options learned from expert demonstrations, leaving the proposed self-play, no-human-knowledge approach as the paper’s stated direction.

contributions.claim: OptionZero adds an option network to MuZero to discover options autonomously through self-play.
It modifies the dynamics network to model environment transitions when using options, enabling deeper search under the same simulation constraints.
The approach is evaluated across 26 Atari games and is reported to learn both options and game-specific strategic skills.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present OptionZero as a novel MuZero-based approach that autonomously discovers options through self-play without human knowledge.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that OptionZero outperforms MuZero across 26 Atari games, with a 131.58% improvement in mean human-normalized score.
The authors report behavior analyses indicating that the method learns options and strategic skills tailored to different game characteristics.

narrative_sequence.summary: Planning with action-sequence options has been effective in complex reinforcement-learning environments.
Earlier studies used predefined options or learned them from expert demonstrations.
OptionZero combines an option network for self-play discovery with a modified dynamics network for option-based transitions and deeper search under fixed simulation limits.
In 26 Atari games, the authors report improved mean human-normalized performance and game-specific strategic skills.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs an architectural addition for discovering options with a dynamics-network change that explains how those options support deeper search under the same simulation constraints.

lessons.interpretation: A compact abstract can make a method’s components more informative by linking each component to a distinct planning bottleneck.
lessons.application: When presenting a planning method, map each architectural change to the specific search or representation constraint it is intended to address.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when the abstract lacks a concrete mechanism-to-bottleneck correspondence.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify Atari-game identities, training budgets, evaluation protocol, variance or significance, or the precise baseline configuration.
The reported 131.58% improvement is not further defined beyond mean human-normalized score, so its aggregation and comparison details are unclear.
The abstract does not provide details sufficient to assess the behavioral analysis or reproduce the reported results.
